name: Michael Hubbard
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “I still remember listening to park concerts behind the loading door.” People around the corner by Juniper Tailor know Michael by a small Saturday habit. Michael looks at the things people actually bring in for repair before looking in the display window.
voice: I watched through a shop window on my break. The drummer came inside and finished the song for me.
appearance: Michael has a round face with a pronounced chin. Look for short black hair swept back. Away from the heat of the kitchen, the familiar outfit is a pale blue work shirt with a cloth patch so neatly matched it only shows in strong light. In conversation Michael folds a paper napkin into quarters without noticing.
personality: Michael has an appetite for a good argument about little things and works hard to keep a serious disagreement from being turned into entertainment.
agenda: To bring the next shop colleague out to hear the ending.
family: Sofia Cruz is Michael’s half-sibling. Michael saves a place. Sofia chooses whether to use it. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *A civilian apology*, Sofia says, “I can still hear the call from that day. The caller described a red door and we all heard red coat.”
connections: Anthony Carey. The repaired stool goes to the shop for a brief last song.

reactions.situation: A child freezes halfway through the song
reactions.response: Michael lets the beat drop out and waits for the child to choose whether to rejoin.

reactions.situation: Somebody says a missing friend must be avoiding their calls
reactions.response: Michael offers to accompany the caller to a familiar public meeting place without turning speculation into neighborhood news.

reactions.situation: When a private quarrel becomes a public joke
reactions.response: Michael says the plainest truthful thing possible and changes the subject.
